AfterObtained.maps_to: no counterpart -- cauldron.py implements no methods at all
AfterObtained.issue: Rollup of guard G1 per binding rule 4. Cauldron.cs:31-34 offers DynamicVars['Potions'].IntValue == 5 PotionRewards on pickup; the port is a behaviourless stub and the player gets nothing.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the stub's premise -- 'out-of-combat pickup effect, stub' -- is false; the sim dispatches after_obtained and has a full potion pipeline
guards.issue: MECHANISM: Cauldron.cs:31-55 builds five PotionRewards (the shipping arm is `new PotionReward(base.Owner)` x 5; the fixed Flex/Weak/Vulnerable/Strength/Dexterity list at :16-23 is the TestMode arm, see G2) and hands them to RewardsCmd.OfferCustom. cauldron.py declares nothing but its id, name, rarity and pickup flag. PREMISE CHECKED (PROMPT.md bug class 12, and `py tools/audit/relic_probes.py sweep-stub-premises` reaches the same conclusion mechanically): RunState.add_relic calls `relic.after_obtained(self)` at run.py:552, so the sim already invokes the exact method the port declines to write, and the potion machinery it would need is live -- `RunState.random_potion` (run.py:513), `RunState.add_potion` (run.py:474), `potion_pools.generate_random_potion` with a real rarity roll, and a rewards screen that already offers potions (rewards.py:466-487). REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- `py tools/audit/relic_probes.py batch3`): `run.add_relic('cauldron')` leaves the belt at [None, None, None] while the same probe shows `run.random_potion() -> 'liquid_memories'` works and add_potion is callable. Cauldron is Shop rarity in the transcribed grab bag (confirmed by `batch3-pool`), so a shop visit with 150-ish gold reaches it. SCOPE NOTE: the shared contract defers potions, but binding rule 1 is explicit that 'the sim has no such system' is a dormant gap and not a waiver -- and here the system is not even missing, only unused. Same handling as relic/belt_buckle's AfterPotionProcured, which was filed as a gap for the same reason.

guards.what: G2: the TestMode arm (Cauldron.cs:16-23, 40-46) is not the shipping behaviour
guards.rationale: Recorded because the sibling relic in this very batch, relic/calling_bell, ported the TestMode arm of the identical OfferCustom pattern by mistake (its guard G1). Cauldron's test arm hands out FlexPotion/WeakPotion/VulnerablePotion/StrengthPotion/DexterityPotion in order; the shipping arm at :48-52 is five unpopulated PotionRewards, each of which rolls from the potion pool. `TestMode.TurnOnInternal` (TestMode.cs:38) has no caller under src/, so the shipping arm is what a fix must implement. Verdict faithful because the port implements neither arm -- there is nothing here to be wrong about beyond G1.
